title: A check counts what should be there
statement: Give a check an expected count from the content, code or a fixed list, never from what it finds, and fail by name on anything missing or unknown.
example: A test script driving a lesson reported 0 problems while leaving one item unanswered; only an unrelated count, reading 6 of 7, showed it.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build's rulebook found that an assertion over everything a walker found is true whenever it finds nothing: after an interaction changed shape, a walker reported every gate answered with 0 problems while leaving an item unanswered, and only an unrelated count of answered items, reading 6 of 7, showed it. The fix has the walk say how many items it reached and compares that with a number taken from the content, never from the walk's own tally, and ends the type dispatch with a branch that names any new item type instead of skipping it. The rulebook generalises that a check walking what it found notices things appearing but never disappearing, so a table of expected things needs assertions in both directions; a Grade 5 course's science gate likewise holds its fixed list of 27 passage IDs apart from the scope ledger, so deleting a row cannot hide a lesson. The Grade 3 package derives its response floors from the player's own call sites and the authored content rather than pinning them, so a response kind the table doesn't know fails by name instead of being under-counted.
against: A count taken from content the delivery code never consults can agree with the bug: "Deriving a count from content the player does not consult is not the conservative choice; it makes the gate agree with the bug." (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md`, lines 622-623).
